claude.sample_unit: MRI scans/participants (259 dementia cases, 259 matched controls)
models_evaluated: RBF support vector machine with distance-from-hyperplane reject option

links.outcome: Leakage-free validation using nested cross-validation with feature selection restricted to training data
links.effect: Nested 5x5 cross-validation, t-test feature reduction applied only to training data; average AUC 0.71, accuracy 66.8% (internal validation only; no external or temporal test set).
links.quote: The t-test was applied only to training data to avoid data leakage, produced a t-map indicating voxel significance between groups, avoiding double dipping.

links.outcome: Accuracy of predictions stratified by distance-from-hyperplane patient-level confidence
links.effect: Confidence-based stratification identified a high-confidence subgroup of ~35% of scans with accuracy ~80%, versus 66.8% overall accuracy (AUC 0.71) across all scans.
links.quote: This strategy allows the model to prioritise high confidence classifications, achieving approximately 80 percent accuracy for one third of scans while maintaining a consistent baseline performance with AUC equal to 0.71 across the entire dataset.

links.outcome: Reporting of uncertainty (confidence intervals) for performance metrics
links.effect: Confidence intervals were not estimated; only fold-level variability was reported, and no subgroup calibration was reported.
links.quote: Confidence intervals were not estimated due to the nested cross validation framework; however, variability across outer folds is reported to provide an indication of model stability and uncertainty.

links.outcome: Performance across heterogeneous scanners and sites
links.effect: Scans came from heterogeneous NHS scanners in one region; the authors claim consistent performance across them but report no separate performance by site or device and list this as a limitation.
links.quote: Routinely collected scans showed heterogeneity in image parameters and equipment, but this was necessary for scaling to a population level.

unlisted_practices: Reject option (selective prediction/deferral) using distance-from-hyperplane threshold to trade coverage for accuracy
Manual expert review of routine MRI scans to exclude artefacts before model training
Secure trusted research environment with disclosure checks on exported results

models_evaluated: Radial Basis Function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) with distance-from-hyperplane confidence calibration

links.effect: Average AUC 0.71 and accuracy 66.8% across five outer folds.
links.quote: The RBF-SVM model performance across five outer folds of the nested cross-validation demonstrated an average AUC score of 0.71 and accuracy of 66.8% in discriminating between scans labelled as future dementia cases and controls as illustrated in Fig. 3 (B).

links.effect: High-confidence classifications achieved approximately 80% accuracy for one third of scans; baseline AUC 0.71.
links.quote: This strategy allows the model to prioritise high confidence classifications, achieving approximately 80 percent accuracy for one third of scans while maintaining a consistent baseline performance with AUC equal to 0.71 across the entire dataset.

links.effect: Prediction accuracy increased to around 80% within a high-confidence subgroup comprising approximately 35% of scans, compared to 66.8% baseline accuracy across all data.
links.quote: Confidence-based stratification identified a high-confidence subgroup comprising approximately 35% of scans, within which prediction accuracy increased to around 80%.
